title: Aborrajados (Colombian cheese-stuffed fried ripe plantain)

ingredients.name: very ripe plantains, with yellow-black skins
mozzarella or queso blanco, cut into 8 sticks

steps: Peel the plantains and cut each in half lengthways, cutting almost through to make a pocket, or slice into thick lengthways pieces.
Fry them in a little oil until golden, then drain and flatten lightly.
Place a stick of cheese, and a bit of guava paste if using, inside each plantain half and fold or pinch together to enclose.
Whisk the flour, egg, water, baking powder and salt to a smooth batter the thickness of cream.
Dip each stuffed plantain in the batter to coat well, and fry in oil at 175 C for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Arroz atollado (Valle del Cauca soupy rice with pork, chicken and potato)

ingredients.name: pork ribs or pork shoulder, in pieces

steps: Season the pork and chicken with salt, pepper and cumin. Brown them in the oil in a wide, heavy pot, then remove.
Fry the chorizo, onion, garlic and tomatoes with the achiote for 6 to 8 minutes.
Return the pork and cover with stock; simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the potatoes, rice and chicken, bring to a simmer and cook gently, covered, for about 25 minutes. The rice should stay moist and soupy, almost like a risotto.
Add a little more stock if it gets dry, stir in coriander and spring onion and serve.

title: Bandeja paisa (Antioquian platter of beans, rice, pork and plantain)

ingredients.name: pork belly in one piece, with skin if available
ground beef or thin beef steak
hogao (tomato and spring onion sauce) to serve

steps: Cook the soaked beans with the carrot, half the onion, garlic and a piece of pork belly for about 1.5 hours until soft, salting near the end; the beans should be thick and tender.
Cut the remaining pork belly into strips, season, and fry slowly in its own fat until crisp and golden. Drain.
Season the ground beef with salt and pepper and fry or grill it until browned; or grill the steak.
Fry or grill the chorizos until cooked through, and fry the plantain slices until golden brown.
Fry the eggs sunny side up.
Serve everything on one large plate: rice, beans, pork, beef, chorizo, plantain, egg, avocado and an arepa, with hogao spooned over the beans and rice.

title: Caldo de costilla (Colombian beef rib broth with potato)

ingredients.name: beef short ribs, cut in pieces

steps: Put the ribs in a large pot with the water, onion, garlic and cumin and bring to a boil, skimming off the foam.
Simmer, partially covered, for 1.5 hours until the ribs are tender.
Add the potatoes and spring onion and cook for 20 minutes until the potatoes are soft and the broth is rich.
Season with salt and pepper and stir in half the coriander.
Ladle into bowls with a rib in each and the rest of the coriander. Serve with arepas or bread, traditionally as a morning meal.

title: Carimañolas (Caribbean-coast Colombian cassava turnovers filled with meat)
steps: Boil the yuca in salted water for 20 to 25 minutes until tender. Drain, remove the fibrous core, and mash with the butter and salt until you have a smooth dough.
Cook the onion and garlic in a little oil, then add the beef, cumin, tomato and salt and cook for 10 minutes until dry. Stir in coriander and cool.
Take a handful of cassava dough, flatten into a disc in your palm, add a spoonful of filling and fold the edges over to form a torpedo shape, sealing well.
Heat oil to 175 C and deep-fry the carimañolas for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with hogao or a lime and coriander dip.

title: Changua (Bogotá milk and egg breakfast soup)

ingredients.name: stale bread rolls or 4 slices bread, in pieces

steps: Bring the water to a boil with the white parts of the spring onions and the salt, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the milk and heat gently until it just comes to a simmer; do not let it boil hard.
Gently crack an egg into the broth for each serving and poach for 3 to 4 minutes until the white is set but the yolk is still soft.
Toast or butter the bread pieces and divide them among 4 bowls.
Ladle the soup with an egg into each bowl and top with the green spring onion and coriander.

title: Enyucado (Caribbean Colombian coconut and cassava cake)

ingredients.name: queso costeño or mild feta, crumbled

steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and grease a loaf tin.
Mix the grated cassava with the coconut, sugar, cheese, melted butter, egg, aniseed, vanilla and salt until evenly combined.
Spoon half the mixture into the tin; add a layer of guava paste if using; then top with the remaining mixture.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes until golden on top and firm in the middle.
Cool for at least 30 minutes before slicing; it is also good cold.

title: Hogao (Colombian tomato and spring onion cooking sauce)

ingredients.name: spring onions (white and light green), finely chopped
ripe tomatoes, peeled and finely chopped

steps: Heat the oil over medium heat and add the spring onions, cooking for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cumin and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomatoes with salt and pepper and cook for about 10 minutes, mashing slightly, until the mixture is jammy and thick.
Stir in the coriander off the heat. Use as a base for stews and rice, or as a sauce for potatoes, beans and arepas.

title: Pandebono (Colombian cheese and cassava starch rolls)

ingredients.name: queso fresco or cuajada, finely grated

steps: Heat the oven to 200 C and line a baking tray.
Mix the cassava starch, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Add the cheese and mix with your hands until crumbly, then add the egg, butter and milk, kneading until you have a smooth, soft dough.
Shape into small balls or rings, about 5 cm wide, and place them on the tray.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until puffed and golden. Serve warm with coffee or hot chocolate.
